newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia blocks use of new drug crop herbicide.
newsitem.headline: Colombia blocks use of new drug crop herbicide.

text.p: Colombia's environment minister on Monday blocked the use of a new U.S.-made chemical to destroy illicit drug plantations because of its harmful side-effects.

Eduardo Verano de la Rosa told reporters he would not permit the use of tebutiron, a granular herbicide, to spray coca leaf and opium poppy crops because studies by his ministry showed it could pose serious health risks for people nearby.
"We will not permit the use of this (chemical) because of indications about possible harmful effects," he said.
Justice Minister Almabeatriz Rengifo and Yvonne Alcala, head of the National Anti-Drug Council, recently approved field trials using tebutiron.
Verano was due to meet U.S. embassy officials Tuesday to discuss his ministry's study on the herbicide.
At present Colombia's anti-drug squad use glyphosate -- a liquid herbicide -- for aerial spraying of coca, the raw material for cocaine, and poppies, used in heroin production.
But heavy rains in the area where drug crops are typically grown reduce its effectiveness because it is quickly washed away, unlike more expensive granular herbicides.

Colombia's U.S.-backed drug crop eradication programme is the most ambitious in Latin America. With the help of U.S. pilots, it last year fumigated more than 9,800 acres (4,000 hectares) of poppy and 44,500 acres (18,000 hectares) of coca.
